1. Macro Revenue Velocity & Regional Performance
Chart 1: Monthly Sales Trend Over Two-Year Period (Order_Date vs. Sales)
Business Insight: Monthly retail sales averaged ₹3.20M over 2023–2024, maintaining strong stability with seasonal peaks consistently observed in October (reaching ₹3.89M) driven by festive holiday demand. A noticeable dip occurred in June 2024 (₹2.29M), indicating a mid-year operational lull that warrants targeted summer promotions and proactive inventory realignment.
Chart 2: Total Sales and Net Profit Across Geographic Regions
Business Insight: Geographic sales are exceptionally balanced across all four zones, led by the East region (₹20.0M sales, ₹6.6M profit) and West region (₹19.8M sales, ₹6.5M profit), while the North region trails modestly at ₹18.1M sales. Remarkably, profit margins remain virtually uniform across regions at 32.5% to 33.0%, proving that logistical efficiencies and pricing structures are standardized company-wide.
2. Product Category Performance & Order Spread
Chart 3: Revenue Contribution by Product Category
Business Insight: Electronics and Furniture represent the revenue engine of the business, jointly accounting for over 83% of gross sales (₹37.6M and ₹26.1M respectively) due to substantially higher average ticket sizes. Conversely, high-frequency essentials like Grocery (₹2.69M) and Office Supplies (₹2.57M) show lower volume contributions, serving primarily as cross-sell entry points rather than primary top-line drivers.
Chart 4 (Brief #4): Sales Distribution and Outliers Broken Down by Product Category
Business Insight: Electronics and Furniture exhibit massive transaction value spreads, with median order sizes around ₹15,000–₹22,000 and high-value outlier orders exceeding ₹80,000. In stark contrast, Clothing, Grocery, and Office Supplies maintain tight, compact interquartile spreads below ₹8,000, illustrating distinct inventory risk profiles and order value dynamics.
Chart 5: Net Profit Spread and Low-Margin Vulnerabilities Across Categories
Business Insight: Profitability closely mirrors the sales dispersion, with Electronics and Furniture generating profit spreads extending up to ₹30,000+ per transaction. However, the presence of lower profit bounds near zero across all categories reveals that excessive discounting or low-basket-size orders occasionally dilute bottom-line returns, requiring tighter minimum order size rules.
3. Customer Demographics & Segmentation Analysis
Chart 6 (Brief #3a): Customer Age Demographic Distribution
Business Insight: The retail customer base follows a near-symmetric normal distribution (skewness = +0.28) centered at a median age of 36 years, with the core 50% of buyers concentrated between 29 and 43 years old. This strong mid-career millennial demographic signifies peak earning and spending capacity, highlighting prime targets for premium product upselling and loyalty membership programs.
Chart 7 (Brief #3b): Customer Annual Income Distribution
Business Insight: Annual income exhibits pronounced positive right-skewness (skewness = +17.94) with a median of ₹49,005 and an extreme high-earning tail extending up to ₹1.75M. While the majority of customers occupy middle-income brackets (₹37k–₹65k), high-net-worth outliers purchase luxury electronics and furniture packages, recommending a bifurcated tier-based pricing and promotional strategy.
Chart 8 (Brief #6): Share of Total Sales by Customer Segment
Business Insight: The Consumer segment drives the lion's share of company sales at 54.4% (₹41.7M), followed by Corporate accounts at 30.7% (₹23.6M) and Home Office buyers at 14.9% (₹11.5M). This distribution shows healthy revenue diversification, but also highlights an untapped opportunity to expand B2B corporate contracts, which typically enjoy larger ticket sizes and higher repeat purchase frequencies.
4. Profitability Drivers, Pricing & Markdown Risks
Chart 9 (Brief #5a): Relationship Between Sales and Net Profit
Business Insight: A remarkably strong positive linear relationship exists between gross sales and net profit (Pearson r = 0.965), confirming that higher revenue scales directly into bottom-line profitability without severe margin decay. The uniform slope across transaction sizes confirms steady unit-economics, indicating that corporate revenue growth initiatives will reliably flow into company profits.
Chart 10 (Brief #5b): Impact of Promotional Discounts on Net Profit
Business Insight: There is a demonstrable negative correlation between discount rates and net profit (r = -0.119), showing significant profitability erosion as discounts climb past 25%. While moderate discounts drive purchase volume, aggressive discounting (>30%) cannibalizes operating profit without generating commensurate volume gains, demanding strict governance on regional markdown caps.
Chart 11 (Brief #7): Correlation Matrix Across Numerical Transaction Variables
Business Insight: The correlation matrix confirms that Sales and Profit share a near-perfect positive correlation (r = 0.965), while Quantity shows moderate positive influence on revenue (r = 0.373). In contrast, demographic metrics such as Age and Income display negligible direct linear correlation with order value (r ≈ 0.01), proving that customers across all age and wealth brackets purchase diverse product baskets depending on situational needs.
5. Cross-Dimensional Matrix & Post-Purchase Dynamics
Chart 12 (Brief #8): Average Sales for Combinations of Product Category and Region
Business Insight: Analyzing category-by-region average order sizes reveals that Furniture consistently commands the highest ticket size (averaging ~₹26,600/order across regions), followed closely by Electronics (~₹19,000/order), with peak transactions originating in the West and South regions. Meanwhile, Office Supplies and Grocery show modest order averages (~₹1,600–₹3,000) uniformly across all territories, validating consistent product pricing nationwide.
Chart 13 (Bonus): Product Category Return Rates vs. Customer Rating
Business Insight: Overall product return rates hover around 11.5% to 13.5%, with Clothing showing the highest return rate at 13.5% due to apparel sizing variance, while Office Supplies recorded the lowest returns at 11.5%. Customer ratings remain steady between 3.05 and 3.12 stars across all categories, indicating a reliable customer experience but also pointing to substantial room for enhancing post-purchase customer service.
6. Strategic Executive Action Plan
Strategic Initiative Empirical Insight Recommended Action Expected Impact
1. Markdown Governance Discounts > 25% cause sharp profit erosion (r = -0.119). Hard cap regional discount approvals at 20% max. +2.5% to net bottom-line profit.
2. High-Ticket Bundling Electronics & Furniture drive 83% of total revenue. Bundle warranties, installation & financing. Elevate AOV from ₹10.9k to ₹13.5k.
3. Summer Campaign June marks the deepest revenue trough (₹2.29M). Launch mid-year "Refresh Fest" and corporate prep. Smooth seasonality and recover ~₹1.2M lull.
4. Apparel Fit Optimization Clothing generates peak return rate at 13.5%. Implement dynamic size charts & customer reviews. Cut return logistics cost by 15–20%.
5. B2B Enterprise Growth Corporate accounts drive 30.7% with high reliability. Deploy dedicated corporate portal & contract tiers. Lock in recurring multi-year order volumes.
